evidence: 1) task/tests/scoring.toml:1-11 is byte-identical to the frozen template (diff empty; sha256 95f70d6e...bbba): [gates] render = 0.0, constraints = 0.0; [weights] functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2 (sum 1); [floors] functional = 0.05. Gates appear only in [gates], never in [weights], so they carry no reward mass. 2) task/tests/tools/score.py is byte-identical to the template (sha256 13de2b38...c04e). Line 41 gates_passed = all(scores[k] > floor); line 42 scored_ran = gates_passed and scored_data is not None; line 44 zeroes weighted dimensions when scored did not run; line 47 floors_passed requires scored_ran and functional > 0.05; line 48 reward = weighted only if gates_passed and floors_passed else 0.0; line 83 returns exit 1 on gate failure. 3) task/tests/test.sh (byte-identical to template, sha256 bd682592...a5aa) lines 212-227: rm -rf scored log; run_suite gates 1500 (failure/timeout -> exit 0 with the pre-written zero record from write_zero_reward at line 60); score.py exit 1 -> 'exit 0' BEFORE run_suite scored 11100 (scored suite skipped); other exit codes -> write_zero_reward. So gates apply before shaping. 4) Executed the frozen score.py (copied to scratchpad, python -I -B, synthetic RewardKit outputs; evidence/43/score_py_simulation.txt sha256 5651b7c2...6f7e): render=0 with a perfect scored file present -> reward 0.0, exit 1, functional/polish/visual forced 0; constraints=0 -> reward 0.0, exit 1; gates pass + functional 0 + polish 0.5 + visual 1.0 (a gate-passing but non-working app farming visual/polish) -> weighted 0.3 but reward 0.0, floors_passed 0; functional 0.0574 (one criterion) + visual 1 -> reward 0.2344; all 1 -> 1.0; missing gate key -> exit 2 -> test.sh writes plain zero. 5) Floor vs criterion granularity: functional judge.toml weights sum to 61 (4.5,7,4,5.5,5,7,4,4.5,6,5.5,3.5,4.5); the smallest criterion (hro_unread_seen 3.5) is 0.0574 > 0.05, so the floor is cleared only by passing at least one whole functional criterion. Every functional criterion requires substantial working behaviour beyond what the gates prove (e.g. hro_intake_restart needs refusals of blank/0/51/2.5 places, Recruiter-as-manager replay, case-insensitive duplicate email refusal and restart_app durability; hro_unread_seen needs live unread counts and seen marks), so an app that only signs in and saves a card (enough for both gates) gets functional 0 and reward 0 regardless of visual/polish. Polish criteria also depend on working live updates/sends, so they cannot be farmed by a shell either. 6) Gates are binary with aggregation all_pass (task/tests/gates/render/judge.toml:14-23, constraints/judge.toml:14-23), one criterion each; they follow lesson 4 (load, reload, server-backed): render = wrong password refused + seeded Recruiter sign-in to a usable workspace; constraints = UI add candidate, reload, independent-context Observer readback. Both prerequisites are public (instruction.md:19 accounts/password; hireops_rules.md:19 'Observer | reads the board...'). Counterexamples tried: (a) plausible broken app that could pass — polished static-ish board with working login and candidate save but no rules/moves/messaging: passes both gates, earns visual ~1 and maybe a polish row, but functional 0 -> floor zeroes reward (verified in execution). (b) conforming alternative that could fail — a correct app whose Observer route is not the default: the gate allows 'another working staff account', so not excluded; a gate judge infra failure returns binary 0 'NOT EXERCISED' and zeroes the reward, which is the template's shared harness behaviour (lesson 11), not a task defect. Notes (non-blocking, P3 at most): the gate judge.toml files carry a comment line 17 '# Criterion weights: 1.0 standard, 1.5 important, 2.0 core...' that is meaningless for all_pass gates (weight = 1 has no reward effect); harmless. The floor margin is narrow (0.0574 vs 0.05) — if a future candidate adds functional criteria so that the smallest weight falls below 5% of the total, a single trivial criterion would still clear the floor; recheck on any functional weight change. Not measured: no configured full-verifier run of test.sh in Docker exercising the gate-fail skip path is present in raw-evidence-index.json (it lists only scripted golden observations); the conclusion rests on byte-identical template code plus direct execution of score.py, which is sufficient for this mechanical row.
